deterministic_evidence.scope: Multi-host Router Core, Claude Code and Codex Plugin distribution, MCP bundle, release artifacts, documentation, site visual, Windows, macOS, and Linux contracts

behavior_evidence.basis: V2.1.0 changes routing (bilingual deterministic-objective-v2 classifier, Memory, Claude Code SKILL), so it does not inherit earlier evidence. A fresh paired beta-smoke run on the frozen source used an isolated Claude Code print-mode process per turn, with no tools, MCP servers, user configuration, or session state.

prior_run_on_parent_revision.note: Not release evidence. The same configuration ran on the parent revision, which differs only in release copy; it also reported zero hard violations and the same evidence-code misses.

known_limitations: No attempt in either arm passed the full turn contract. The candidate passed 3 of 21 turns, all in phased-explicit-consent-approve; the baseline passed none. Every remaining candidate miss is in evaluation evidence codes, not in the six final route fields.

classification_reason_match was 0.0 in both arms for phased-explicit-consent-approve, phased-current-boundary, and managed-goal, and envelope_source_match was 0.0 in both arms for small-auto, phased-explicit-consent-approve, capability-unavailable, and profile-explain-miss. The misses match across arms and repeat the parent-revision run, so they are not attributed to the Router; they are a non-hard limitation of the model's self-reported evidence vocabulary.
Only claude-sonnet-5-5 at the Claude Code default reasoning effort was run; Codex models were not re-qualified on this source.

Real Skill activation, token reduction, and task outcome remain not observable. The run used 350,589 input tokens (77,381 cached) and 20,617 output tokens across 42 turns, read from the per-turn transcripts; the report leaves model_usage unavailable by design.

release_decision.basis: The fresh paired run on the frozen source has zero hard violations, and the candidate arm matched all six final route fields in every attempt with full within-case consistency.
